A_target.statement:
Let $p$ be an [[Definition:Odd Prime|odd prime]] and $a \perp p$.
Then:
:$a^{\frac {p - 1} 2} \equiv \paren {\dfrac a p} \pmod p$
and there are exactly $\dfrac {p - 1} 2$ [[Definition:Quadratic Residue|quadratic residues]] modulo $p$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\phi: G \to H$ be a [[Definition:Group Homomorphism|group homomorphism]].
Then:
:$G / \map \ker \phi \cong \Img \phi$

substitutions.the homomorphism phi: squaring, and then the power map x -> x^((p-1)/2)

object_map.reformulation: Identify the quadratic residues as the image of squaring and as the kernel of the half-order power map.

validity_conditions: Z/pZ is a field, so x^2 = 1 only for x = 1 or -1, and x^((p-1)/2) = 1 has at most (p - 1)/2 roots.
p must be odd so that 1 and -1 are distinct.
proof_plan:
Let $G = \paren {\Z / p \Z}^\times$, of order $p - 1$, and $\map s x = x^2$.
In the field $\Z / p \Z$, $x^2 = 1$ {{iff}} $x = \pm 1$, so $\map \ker s = \set {\pm 1}$.
By the source result, the group $Q = \Img s$ of quadratic residues has $\dfrac {p - 1} 2$ elements.

Let $\map h x = x^{\frac {p - 1} 2}$.
Then $\map h x^2 = x^{p - 1} = 1$, so $\map h x = \pm 1$, and $\map h {y^2} = y^{p - 1} = 1$, so $Q \subseteq \map \ker h$.
As $x^{\frac {p - 1} 2} - 1$ has at most $\dfrac {p - 1} 2$ roots, $\map \ker h = Q$.
